Alex: Heads up — after the runtime deploy at ~2134000000 we're seeing a pretty regular sawtooth in tail latency + intermittent throughput drops. p50 looks fine but p95/p99 jump every ~25-35s. Rolling back binary removes the pattern. Opening thread to correlate kernel selection, batching, and KV cache.
Sara: Thanks — do we have a dashboard link and any KV eviction metrics? :eyes:
Alex: Dashboard: https://dashboards.internal/redwood/runtime/sawtooth-2134
Alex: Quick snapshot from last 10m: 
```
p50: 18ms
p95: 220ms (oscillates 80ms -> 420ms)
p99: 980ms (spikes aligned to sawtooth)
throughput: -12% during spikes
microbatch_size hist: bimodal -> peaks at 1 and 8
kv_cache_evictions/sec: baseline 6 -> spike 120
kernel_selector log: fused_kernel -> fallback_kernel flip every ~28s
```
Max: Interesting — bimodal microbatching + kernel flip smells like admission window jitter + kernel thresholding. Any recent config changes to admission or kernel thresholds?
Jon: We deployed a minor change to admission.min_batch_ms in the same release: 6 -> 2 to reduce latency for small requests. Also adjusted kernel_selector.thresholds for fused kernels (batch_size >= 4).
Maya: Memory ledger shows periodic compaction/flush events at same cadence (every ~28s) when resident set crosses high-watermark. That compaction does KV eviction for LRUK entries.
Alex: So timeline: smaller min_batch_ms -> more microbatches of size 1-2 -> kernel_selector sees too-small batches and falls back to slower kernel -> longer tails -> KV cache high-water triggers ledger flush -> mass evictions -> next few requests miss cache and latencies jump -> admission tries to absorb but microbatching stays fragmented -> repeat.
Sara: That matches: eviction spikes precede p99 spikes by ~1-2s in traces. Any profiling of kernel latencies by batch size?
Alex: Yes, quick profile: 
```
batch_size | fused_ms | fallback_ms
1          | 12       | 20
4          | 10       | 35
8          | 9        | 40
```
When selector flips to fallback for size 1-2 we actually see worse latency compared to fused for moderate sizes due to kernel warmup/cold paths.
Max: So the selector's decision boundary + admission change created a pathological regime. Two levers: raise min_batch_ms back or change kernel selector to prefer fused for small seq lengths even when batch<4.
Jon: Quick mitigation: rolling back admission.min_batch_ms to 6 is low-risk and quick. For longer-term, we should update kernel_selector to use a heuristic that uses recent kernel latency histograms per shard (not fixed thresholds) and add hysteresis to avoid flip-flopping.
Maya: Also recommend delaying ledger compaction until after a grace window when admission has stabilized, or use adaptive eviction backoff to avoid mass evictions caused by transient bursts.
Sara: Can we ship rollback now? I can trigger. @deploy-bot do we have a one-click rollback for the runtime agent? :pray:
deploy-bot: rollback job queued: runtime-agent:v2134000000 -> runtime-agent:v2133998000. Estimated ETA 2m.
Alex: I'll watch traces and KV metrics. If rollback removes sawtooth, we can revert faster.
perf-bot: Alert: sawtooth latency pattern detected -> replayed to perf-channel. Noting correlation with admission.min_batch_ms change.
Max: Action items: 1) rollback (Sara) 2) add kernel_selector hysteresis + dynamic hist buckets (Jon/Maya) 3) add eviction backoff in ledger (Maya) 4) add test harness to simulate admission jitter vs kernel selection (Alex/Max).
Sara: Rollback completed, routing traffic back to v2133998000.
perf-bot: Metrics update 30s after rollback: p95 down from 420ms -> 60ms, p99 down from 980ms -> 160ms, kv_evictions/sec back to baseline ~7.
Alex: Nice — rollback cleared the sawtooth. Keeping thread open for follow-ups on selector hysteresis and ledger fixes.
Jon: I'll open a PR for selector hysteresis + small e2e that simulates microbatch fragmentation.
Maya: I'll prototype eviction backoff and a ledger soft-threshold.
Max: I'll add a chaos test to perf harness to vary min_batch_ms and kernel thresholds and assert no sawtooth under realistic load.
Alex: Thanks everyone. Will add postmortem note after we have PRs and perf tests. :thumbsup:
